collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older and a young carver or another adult)

collection.description: A villager who never became the best carver watches a young carver do better: say it is beautiful, or walk away for a while.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, (subject.he/she) wanted more than anything to be the best carver on Isola. (subject.He/she) practiced for years. (subject.He/she) was good. Never the best. Today (subject.he/she) is watching (friend), a young carver, finish a piece that is better than anything (subject) ever made. (subject.He/she) feels a sharp little sting, even after all these years.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) walks away, out to the beach, and lets (subject.him/her)self feel it: the old wanting, the disappointment, the little bit of jealousy. (subject.He/she) doesn't pretend it's not there. After a while, it settles. (subject.He/she) still carves, sometimes, for fun. (subject.He/she) goes home and carves something small and silly. It's not the best. (subject.He/she) likes it.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells (friend) it's beautiful, and means it, even with the sting. (friend) beams. "Did you carve too?" asks (friend). "I did," says (subject). "Not like that." (subject.He/she) shows (friend) an old piece of (subject.his/her) own. (friend) studies it seriously and says it has something (friend.his/her) own doesn't. (subject) isn't sure that's true, but it's kind. The sting is still there. That's alright.
